sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2024 fluvial gathering
sources.note: Reports 1.5 million devotees and a concluding Basilica Pontifical Mass. The crowd layout and ninety-minute Mass are illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: updated 2026 fluvial schedule
sources.note: 2026 advisory: departure 21:00; estimated Mass start 23:00. Illustrative annual replay: river 16:00–18:00, Mass 18:00–19:30.

sources.title: City of Naga: 2022 fluvial procession and concluding Mass
sources.note: Documents the foot procession after the 14:00 Cathedral Mass and the concluding Mass; does not establish a 16:00 fluvial departure.

sources.title: OSM Basilica Loop and owner annotation
sources.note: OSM Basilica Loop curb; owner annotation, 2026-10-07: main loop and short northern pieces, offset four metres outward from the mapped six-metre carriageway centreline. On 2026-10-08 the owner limited the crowd to the forecourt: the boundary is cut along the south curb of Basilica Road (OSM way 23523456), in front of the facade. The whole annotated loop remains the car-free traffic closure, with its parking emptied of cars.

sources.title: Daily Tribune: 2026 Traslación
sources.note: Reports both images reaching Porta Mariae around 18:30, followed by Holy Mass, with about 820,000 devotees. The number drawn is illustrative.

sources.title: Project owner: Cathedral precinct annotation
sources.note: Project owner annotated atlas image, 2026-10-07. Boundary fitted around the annotated forecourt with a four-metre curb margin. On 2026-10-08 the owner removed the illustrative outdoor altar stage and the crowd from the Archbishop's Residence garden (OSM way 1314309818), whose west edge now bounds the crowd; placement is approximate, not a surveyed festival arrangement.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2026 festival calendar
sources.note: Dated event dates and starts. Annual recurrence and depicted formations are illustrative; future arrangements may vary.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: parade traffic advisory and official map
sources.note: Parade traffic advisory for the festival week; road closures and timing. The depicted loop follows the owner-supplied official route map below.

sources.title: Project owner: official parade route map
sources.note: Official 15th Bicol Regional Military Parade route map supplied by the project owner, 2026-10-08: west on Panganiban Drive from the crossing rotonda, across the bridge, south on Dinaga, west on Padian (OSM Caceres Street), north on General Luna, east on Kinastillohan, south on Elias Angeles, east on Panganiban, north on Peñafrancia Avenue and west on P. Burgos to the plaza. Matched to OSM ways by the atlas.

sources.title: Philippine Information Agency: 72 contingents in 2023
sources.note: Reports 72 contingents in the September 15, 2023 competition; this does not assert the same count in every year.

sources.title: City of Naga: 2023 parade event window
sources.note: The September 15, 2023 event lists 07:00–10:00. The 2026 start remains 07:00; the replay length is illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: fluvial route advisory
sources.note: Cathedral to Danlugan ni Ina, the river and the Basilica. River geometry comes from OSM; the rendered flotilla and spectators are illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: updated 2026 fluvial schedule
sources.note: River conditions moved the 2026 departure to 21:00; ninety minutes on the water was estimated. The annual 16:00–18:00 replay is illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2024 fluvial gathering
sources.note: Reports 1.5 million devotees and a concluding Pontifical Mass at the Basilica. Flotilla and crowds are illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Ordinance 582, section 2(23)
sources.note: Connects Santonja Street to Colgante Bridge. Matching this location to OSM way 23540251 is a geographic inference.

sources.title: Dennis T. Marpuri: Colgante eyewitness account
sources.note: January 2026 account associates former Colgante Street with present Santoja Street; corroborates the mapped bridge alias.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2026 Dagsaan landing
sources.note: September 20, 2026: Dagsaan landing near the Basilica, about 1.2 million spectators. The night schedule differs from the illustrative afternoon replay.

sources.title: Project owner: Dagsaan landing crowd annotation
sources.note: Project owner annotated atlas image, 2026-10-08: crowd on the landing ground by footway 1203053284, about 50 m of Balatas-Cararayan Road beside it and Basilica Loop's west leg to Basilica Road, which close to cars during the replay. Rings fitted to the annotation and OSM road geometry; placement is approximate.

sources.title: Bicol Mail: 2026 Traslación streets
sources.note: Reports a noon Shrine departure and the named street sequence. Iglesia Road is represented by the mapped Paz/Callejon segment adjacent to Porta Mariae; this mapping uses OSM geography.

sources.title: Project owner: Archbishop's Residence grounds
sources.note: On 2026-10-08 the project owner asked for no crowd in the Archbishop's Residence grounds; the roadside and Cathedral Grounds crowds stop at the mapped garden outline.
